# **Assignment No. 2**

## VoltGrid: EV Charging Network & Fleet Energy Management System

# **Aim**

To study the standard structure of a Software Requirements Specification (SRS) and to prepare a complete SRS document for the proposed VoltGrid platform, following the IEEE 830 / ISO-IEC-IEEE 29148 hybrid template. The document captures the functional and non-functional requirements, external interfaces, system architecture, data requirements, quality attributes, risks, and project plan for the system.

## **Software Requirements Specification (SRS)**

**Project Title:** VoltGrid – EV Charging Network & Fleet Energy Management System

**Prepared by:** Aryan Suryawanshi, Soham Kulkarni, Sarang Kolekar, Prathmesh Naik (Department of Information Technology, PCCOE)

**Document Version:** v1.0

**Date:** 23/07/2026

# **1\. Introduction**

## **1.1 Purpose**

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) describes the functional and non-functional requirements of VoltGrid, an enterprise EV Charging Network Operations & Fleet Energy Management Platform. It defines what the system must do, the constraints under which it must operate, and the interfaces it must support, so that the development team, testers, and evaluators share a common and unambiguous understanding of the product. The intended audience includes the project development team, the project guide and examiners, quality-assurance/testing members, and the platform stakeholders (EV drivers, charging-station operators, fleet managers, and system administrators).

## **1.2 Document Conventions**

This document follows the IEEE 830 / ISO-IEC-IEEE 29148 SRS conventions. The following conventions are used throughout:

•**Roles:** Driver, Operator, Fleet Manager, and Administrator refer to the five user classes defined in Section 2.3.

## **1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions**

•**Developers:** Sections 3 (functional requirements), 4 (interfaces), 6 (architecture), and 7 (data) for implementation detail.

•**Testers / QA:** Sections 3, 5 (non-functional requirements), and 8 (quality attributes) to derive test cases.

•**Stakeholders / end users:** Sections 1.4 (product scope), 2.2 (features), and 2.3 (user classes) for a functional overview.

## **1.4 Product Scope**

VoltGrid is a centralized platform that manages electric-vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure end-to-end. It enables EV drivers to locate and reserve charging stations, run and monitor charging sessions, make secure digital payments through an in-app wallet, and report charger faults. It provides dedicated portals for charging-station operators, fleet managers, and administrators to monitor station performance, manage maintenance, analyze energy usage, and oversee overall network operations. The expected benefits are higher charger utilization, reduced downtime through structured fault handling, transparent billing, and data-driven operational decisions across the EV charging network.

# **2\. Overall Description**

## **2.1 Product Perspective**

VoltGrid is a new, self-contained product rather than a component of an existing system. It follows a decoupled client-server architecture: a React.js \+ Tailwind CSS single-page application (SPA) on the front end communicates with a Python (FastAPI) REST API backend, which persists data in a PostgreSQL database through the SQLAlchemy ORM. A WebSocket channel pushes real-time charger/kiosk state to clients. The system is containerized with Docker and built/tested through GitHub Actions CI/CD for consistent deployment and horizontal scaling. Externally, VoltGrid interfaces with a digital payment gateway for wallet top-ups, a maps/geolocation service for station discovery, charger hardware behaviour is provided by a Software-based Kiosk Telemetry Emulator Engine (see Section 2.6)

## **2.2 Product Features**

At a high level, VoltGrid provides the following ten functional modules:

•Authentication & Role Management – secure sign-up, login, and role-based access control.

•Charging Station Discovery – search, map view, filtering, and station details.

•Slot Reservation – booking of charging slots with conflict detection.

•Charging Session Management – start/stop sessions and track energy, duration, and cost.

•Wallet & Billing – wallet top-ups, automatic deductions, and invoice generation.

•Fleet Management – dashboards for managing multiple vehicles and drivers.

•Maintenance & Fault Ticketing – fault reporting, ticket assignment

•Community – driver reviews, ratings, and discussion for stations.

•Admin Analytics & Reporting – network-wide monitoring, energy analytics, and reports.

## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics**

•**EV Drivers:** locate/reserve stations, run charging sessions, pay via wallet, and report faults; largest user base, mixed technical skill.

•**Charging Station Operators:** register and manage stations, set pricing/availability, and monitor station performance.

•**Fleet Managers:** manage multiple vehicles and drivers, schedule charging, and view fleet-level usage and billing.

•**System Administrators:** oversee the whole network, manage roles and policies, and access analytics and audit information.

## **2.4 Operating Environment**

•**Client:** any modern web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) on desktop or mobile; responsive UI.

•**Server:** Linux-based host running the Dockerized Python (FastAPI) backend and PostgreSQL database.

•**Network:** HTTPS over the public internet; REST/JSON between the SPA and the API.

•**Deployment:** Docker containers, orchestrated to scale horizontally as stations, fleets, and accounts grow.

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints**

•**Technology stack:** backend in Python with the FastAPI framework; frontend in React.js with Tailwind CSS; PostgreSQL accessed through the SQLAlchemy ORM; WebSockets/Socket.IO for real-time state; Docker with GitHub Actions for packaging, CI/CD, and deployment (see the Technology Stack table in Section 6).

•**Security:** JWT-based authentication and role-based access control (RBAC); passwords stored using a strong one-way hash.

•**Financial integrity:** wallet and billing operations must be transactional (ACID) to prevent incorrect balances.

•**API design:** versioned REST endpoints with a stable contract consumed by the decoupled frontend.

•**Regulatory:** handling of payment and personal data must follow applicable data-protection and payment-security good practice.

## **2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies**

•Users have reliable internet connectivity and a supported browser.

•A third-party payment gateway is available and reliable for wallet top-ups.

•**Kiosk Telemetry Emulator Engine:** in the absence of physical hardware, charger behaviour is simulated by a Software-based Kiosk Telemetry Emulator Engine that streams real-time state-machine updates (Charging\_kWh, PlugDetected, FaultState) to clients over WebSockets, faithfully mimicking hardware transitions. This emulator is the authoritative source of charger state until physical IoT-enabled chargers are integrated, at which point the same WebSocket contract is reused.

•A maps/geolocation provider is available for station discovery.

•Station operators keep station availability, connector, and tariff data up to date.

# **3\. System Features and Functional Requirements**

This section describes each system feature and its functional requirements. 

| Module | Summary |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Authentication & Role Management** | User registration, login using JWT, role-based access control, password reset. |
| **Charging Station Discovery** | Search stations by location, connector type, and availability; view stations on a map with live status. |
| **Slot Reservation** | Reserve charging slots, prevent double booking, modify/cancel reservations, live waitlist when full. |
| **Charging Session Management** | Start/stop charging sessions, monitor energy and cost in real time, manage charger state transitions, handle faults automatically. |
| **Wallet & Billing** | Wallet top-ups, automatic payment deduction, invoice generation, transaction history, prepaid and fleet postpaid billing. |
| **Fleet Management** | Manage fleet vehicles and drivers, bulk scheduling, usage analytics, monthly consolidated billing. |
| **Maintenance & Fault Ticketing** | Report charger faults, automatically generate and manage maintenance tickets. |
| **Community** | Drivers can rate and review charging stations. |
| **Admin Analytics & Reporting** | Network-wide dashboards, energy and revenue reports, export reports for analysis. |

# **4\. External Interface Requirements**

## **4.1 User Interfaces**

The user interface is a responsive React.js \+ Tailwind CSS single-page application with role-specific dashboards, rendering three main views — the Driver (mobile app) view and the Fleet/Admin Dashboard. It provides map-based station discovery, reservation and session screens, a wallet/billing view, and management consoles, with consistent navigation and accessible, mobile-friendly layouts.

## **4.2 Kiosk  Interfaces**

VoltGrid interfaces logically with EV charging hardware (chargers/connectors) to reflect availability and session state. In the initial release this hardware is represented by the Software-based Kiosk Telemetry Emulator Engine, which streams Charging\_kWh, PlugDetected, and FaultState events over WebSockets using the same contract that physical IoT-enabled chargers will later implement, so no application logic changes when real hardware is integrated.

## **4.3 Software Interfaces**

•**Payment gateway:** REST/HTTPS integration for wallet top-ups and payment confirmation.

•**Maps / geolocation service:** for station location, search, and routing on the map view.

•**Database:** PostgreSQL accessed via the SQLAlchemy ORM from the FastAPI backend.

•**Frontend–backend:** versioned REST/JSON API (with FastAPI-generated OpenAPI/Swagger docs) over HTTPS between the React SPA and the FastAPI server.

•**Real-time channel:** a WebSocket/Socket.IO connection for pushing live charger/session state to clients.

## **4.4 Communication Interfaces**

All client-server communication uses HTTPS with TLS. The REST API exchanges JSON payloads, while a WebSocket (RFC 6455\) / Socket.IO channel carries real-time charger and session events. Authentication uses bearer JWT tokens in the HTTP Authorization header. Email/SMS notifications MAY be sent for reservations, low wallet balance, and ticket updates.

# **5\. Non-Functional Requirements**

| Category | Requirement |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Performance** | REST API response \< 200 ms (95th percentile); WebSocket updates \< 100 ms. |
| **Security** | TLS encryption, password hashing, JWT authentication, RBAC, secure financial transactions. |
| **Usability** | Responsive, intuitive interface for desktop and mobile devices. |
| **Reliability** | Target 99% uptime with graceful failure recovery. |
| **Scalability** | Docker-based deployment supporting horizontal scaling as users and stations increase. |
| **Maintainability** | Modular architecture allowing independent updates to system modules. |
| **Availability** | Core services remain operational during maintenance of non-critical modules. |

## **6.1 Technology Stack**

The recommended technology stack for VoltGrid, mapped to each architectural layer:

| Layer | Recommended Technology | Why It Fits VoltGrid |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Backend & APIs | Python (FastAPI) | High speed, built-in async support for WebSockets (simulating kiosk telemetry), and automatic OpenAPI/Swagger documentation for testing. |
| Database Layer | PostgreSQL \+ SQLAlchemy (ORM) | Structured relational model with ACID compliance — essential for transaction logs, per-kWh billing, and wallet balance constraints. |
| Real-Time Simulation | WebSockets / Socket.IO | Models the charger/kiosk hai state machine: pushes real-time PlugDetected, Charging\_kWh, and Error states to the client. |
| Frontend / Dashboards | React.js \+ Tailwind CSS | Clean, component-based UI for the three main views: Driver mobile app and Fleet/Admin Dashboard. |
| Testing Frameworks | PyTest \+ Postman \+ Selenium | Covers backend unit testing, API collection automation, and UI interaction tests. |
| Deployment & CI/CD | Docker \+ GitHub Actions | Containerized deployment with automated build-and-test pipelines. |

# **7\. Data Requirements**

## **7.1 Data ModelsU**

Core entities and their key relationships include:

•**User:** id, name, email, password hash, role, wallet reference.

•**Station:** id, operator, location, set of connectors, assigned TariffPlan, aggregate availability.

•**Connector:** id, station, connector type, power rating (kW), and status (AVAILABLE / RESERVED / OCCUPIED / FAULTED) — the individual charging bay/port that is reserved, occupied, and billed.

•**Reservation:** id, user, connector, time window, status (RESERVED / ACTIVE / EXPIRED / CANCELLED).

•**ChargingSession:** id, reservation, energy delivered, duration, cost, status.

•**Wallet & Transaction:** balance, top-ups, deductions, invoices.

•**FaultTicket:** id, station, reporter, status, SLA timestamps.

•**Fleet:** manager, vehicles, drivers, and aggregated usage.

## **7.2 Data Flow**

Users interact with the app, which sends requests to the backend server. The server checks user permissions and updates the database, keeping all financial steps linked so money is never lost. Meanwhile, live charging updates are pushed to screens in real-time, and session data is automatically saved for administrative reports.

1\. Driver \---\> Sends reservation request \---\> FastAPI Backend \---\> Writes hold constraint \---\> PostgreSQL

2\. Kiosk Emulator \---\> Pushes PlugDetected \= true via WebSocket \---\> FastAPI Backend \---\> Transitions state (RESERVED \---\> ACTIVE)

3\. Kiosk Emulator \---\> Streams Charging\_kWh metrics \---\> React SPA Frontend (Live Display)

4\. Driver / Station \---\> Sends Stop Session trigger \---\> FastAPI Backend

5\. FastAPI Backend \---\> Calculates final cost \---\> Executes Atomic Transaction (Deducts Wallet \+ Generates Invoice) \---\> PostgreSQL

## **7.3 Data Retention and Archival Policies**

Transactional, financial, and operational records are kept for audit and analytics purposes, while personal user data is retained only for active accounts and promptly deleted or anonymized upon account closure.

# **8\. Quality Attributes**

•**Testability:** modular services and versioned REST APIs enable unit testing (PyTest), API collection automation (Postman), and UI interaction tests (Selenium) per module.

•**Modifiability:** the decoupled frontend/backend and independent modules allow features to change with minimal ripple effect.

•**Interoperability:** standard REST/JSON and TLS enable integration with payment, maps, and future IoT systems.

•**Portability:** Docker containerization with GitHub Actions CI/CD makes the system portable across hosting environments with automated build-and-test pipelines.

•**Reliability & Robustness:** transactional financial operations and explicit session edge-case handling protect data integrity.

# **9\. Risk Analysis**

Key risks and their mitigation strategies:

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Incorrect wallet/billing calculation | High – financial loss / user distrust | ACID transactions, automated tests, reconciliation checks |
| Overlapping / duplicate reservations | Medium – disrupted charging schedule | Conflict detection and DB constraints on slot/time |
| Mid-session disconnect or charger fault | Medium – wrong cost / stuck session | Explicit session state machine and edge-case handling |
| Unresolved fault tickets | Medium – chargers offline | SLA-based assignment and escalation workflow |
| Misconfigured RBAC | High – unauthorized access | Centralized RBAC checks and access testing |
| Payment gateway downtime | Medium – top-ups blocked | Retry/queue logic and graceful failure messaging |

# **10\. Project Plan Overview**

## **10.1 Milestones and Timeline**

The project is delivered incrementally across Agile sprints (as selected in Assignment 1):

| Sprint | Milestone | Modules Delivered |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Sprint 1 | Foundation | Authentication & Role Management |
| Sprint 2 | Discovery & Booking | Station Discovery, Slot Reservation |
| Sprint 3 | Core Charging | Charging Session Management |
| Sprint 4 | Payments | Wallet & Billing |
| Sprint 5 | Operations | Fleet Management, Maintenance & Fault Ticketing |
| Sprint 6 | Value-add & Insights | Marketplace, Community, Admin Analytics |

## **10.2 Budget Estimates**

As an academic third-year project, VoltGrid is built with open-source and free-tier tooling (Python/FastAPI, React.js/Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL/SQLAlchemy, Docker, and GitHub Actions). The primary cost is student effort across the six sprints; the only potential recurring costs are optional cloud hosting and a payment-gateway sandbox, both of which have free or low-cost tiers during development.

# **11\. Appendix**

## **Glossary**

•**SRS:** Software Requirements Specification.

•**RBAC:** Role-Based Access Control.

•**JWT:** JSON Web Token, used for authenticated sessions.

•**ORM / SQLAlchemy:** Object-Relational Mapper; SQLAlchemy is the Python ORM used with PostgreSQL.

•**FastAPI:** the Python web framework used for the REST API and WebSocket server.

•**WebSocket:** a persistent, bidirectional channel used to stream real-time charger/session state.

•**CI/CD:** Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment, implemented with GitHub Actions.

•**SLA:** Service Level Agreement, used for fault-ticket resolution times.

•**EV:** Electric Vehicle.

**Kano Model**

| Category | Features from VoltGrid |
| ----- | ----- |
| Must-Be (Basic Needs) | User Authentication & RBAC, Station Discovery, Slot Reservation, Charging Session Management, Wallet & Billing, Secure Payments, Fault Reporting |
| One-Dimensional (Performance Needs) | Real-time Charger Status, Fleet Management Dashboard, Reservation Conflict Detection, Energy Tracking, Billing Reports, Admin Analytics |
| Attractive (Delighters) | Community Reviews & Ratings, Live Virtual Waitlist, Automatic Maintenance Ticket Generation, Fleet Monthly Consolidated Invoice, Real-time WebSocket Updates |
| Indifferent | Choice of Docker, SQLAlchemy, React, FastAPI (implementation details invisible to users) |
| Reverse | None identified |
